title: Quarterly OTC Allowance Loads on Pharmacy Coverage
content:
**Pharmacy Benefit — over-the-counter (OTC) allowance.** Each calendar quarter's over-the-counter allowance is booked on the coverage as one load entry tagged to that quarter.

### When the load amount is fixed

The quarter load is fixed only after the ledger carries a forfeiture entry for the latest quarter loaded before it.

Put the other way round: while the allowance activity of the coverage shows no forfeiture entry tagged to the latest quarter loaded before the new one, the amount of the new quarter load is not yet fixed.

### Business effect

The load adds one load entry to the allowance activity of the member's pharmacy coverage, tagged with the quarter and dated the day it is booked, and raises the coverage's current allowance balance by the loaded amount. Afterwards the member can see the quarter's load in the allowance activity and spend the new balance on catalog items.

### How it is invoked

Loading is an agent-side action. The agent unlocks the tool `load_otc_quarter_30ec28e6` and then calls it.

### Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `rx_coverage_id` | The reference number of the member's pharmacy coverage record, as returned by the pharmacy coverage lookup for the verified member | Identifier, as shown by the lookup |
| `benefit_quarter` | The calendar quarter being loaded | YYYY-Qn (for example 2026-Q3) |
| `load_amount` | The allowance loaded for the quarter | USD, a positive amount with 2 decimal places; a value with more places is rounded to 2 decimal places |

### Return

On success the tool returns a text rendering of `rx_otc_id` (the reference number of the new load entry), `benefit_quarter` (YYYY-Qn), `load_amount` (USD with 2 decimal places), `otc_balance` (the allowance balance after the load, USD with 2 decimal places) and `status` (the text "loaded", which confirms the load was booked).

### Contract notes

*Does one call book more than one quarter?* No. One call books one load entry for the quarter given.

*Does the load replace the existing balance?* No. The balance is raised by the loaded amount.
